claims.statement: TermindApp shares its AppModel and persistence container across main WindowGroup scenes, constructing a fresh WindowModel per ordinary/restored scene (or a demo-configured model for a debug screenshot launch without a request ID); RootView holds the model in @State and provides it to environment and focused scene commands, while the external-authentication Window is excluded from ordinary scene-opening commands.

RootView owns one NavigationSplitView and window toolbar, overlays status on the active workspace without docking it, and places Vault, Assistant, Metrics and Settings in front of a persistent workspace deck.

WindowModel separates destination, sidebar mode, page selections/searches, presentation routes and focused workspace state; user sidebar activation can restore Assistant's prior destination, while History is disallowed for focused Telnet/serial sessions.

The persistent workspace deck retains all open workspace views, gates hidden interaction/accessibility, parks hidden layouts at identity-keyed cached usable sizes, and prunes closed IDs rather than relaying every container resize to hidden split trees.

WorkspaceContentView renders stable-ID split leaves and fraction-based branches, previews divider movement locally, keeps a dragged source mounted while omitting it from preview geometry, and disables hidden-workspace shortcut owners.
Vault list/editor children retain identity across the split breakpoint; a covered list keeps its cached size and editor transitions animate position and reserved space rather than resizing the form.

ManagedCardPage supplies typed sections, stable item IDs, externally owned selection, capabilities and business views to a reusable renderer; drop geometry yields stable-ID mutation intent while resource-specific actions and presentation remain with the page.

The workspace compact Assistant has routing separate from the full Assistant destination and composes transcript/interaction regions with explicit terminal context; Escape cannot fall through from a blocking interaction into closing the conversation.

TFM transcript owners are cached per window by conversation and surface, preserving native list and presentation state across mounts; the default eight-owner LRU trims unmounted candidates without forcibly evicting mounted surfaces.

ResponsivePageLayoutTests includes visible-window-gated narrow editor cases in English and both Chinese variants, while its offscreen Metrics case verifies native table identity, sorting and scroll retention across width changes.

TFM Welcome projects only this installation's recent connection events and uses their local timestamps, while the History sidebar searches the synchronized all-device timeline and caps displayed matches at 100.
Saved-host SSH, Telnet, and SFTP panes own connection-history events; closing ends the event, moving preserves it, and Serial or unsaved targets are excluded.

TFM History rows resolve each event's sourceDeviceID through the reusable app-wide device directory, so the displayed device name follows directory updates rather than remaining a hostname captured inside the event.

On macOS 26+ the native NavigationSplitView owns the Sidebar background with no extra glass overlay; older systems use an AppKit visual-effect fallback. The mode rail uses one glass capsule with a neutral moving highlight, selected accessibility traits, a key-window focus outline and Reduce Motion-aware animation.

Assistant full-screen and compact surfaces share one window-local Archive flag while retaining separate conversation selections; native blank-area menu checkmarks read that flag, but sidebar Show Archive preserves the foreground workspace and full-screen Show Archive changes destination. Compact open/close clears Archive, and the compact archive can explicitly open full screen.

MainWindowCoordinator requests a UUID-valued main scene for moving a workspace and leaves the live workspace in the source until the native destination registers; registration takes and opens the same workspace in the destination model rather than closing and reopening its session.

Closing a registered main window unregisters its model and calls closeForWindow, which disconnects all workspaces and clears window-local reopen, drag, route and transcript cache state; a restored window without a pending request retains its system-restored frame.

The Navigator's workspace inline rename starts with the full localized displayed title before the native field receives focus; commits delegate to WindowModel, which rejects unrenameable workspaces, trims names and stores split-workspace names on the group but single-pane names on the pane.

The Navigator overlays an AppKit-compatible workspace layout drop receiver above native List rows; it uses live window drag state and measured row frames to preview insertion, excluding the dragged workspace when calculating its mutation index, then reorders a workspace or detaches a pane only on a valid drop in Navigator mode.

Workspace row drag state starts on macOS 26 only after the native List drag session becomes active, while older systems set it in onDrag; the model documents that an older release outside a destination can leave stale drag state until the next click/drag, so drop callbacks validate the pasteboard.

Workspace Navigator expansion is a persisted presentation preference, independently of workspace ownership: selecting a Vault or workspace destination expands its section, and its row menu routes selection-sensitive pane actions through the window model.

The Snippets sidebar filters shared host-library snippets with a sidebar-local footer and can insert into a live focused SSH/Telnet terminal; executing a risk-classified snippet requires an additional confirmation. Its persisted package-folding state is distinct from the full Snippets page's expansion.

The History sidebar projects SSH command history, SFTP browse history, or connection history according to the selected workspace's focused pane, while Snippets and History use AppKit ListViewKit-backed rows with separate footer search and blank-area menus rather than changing the titlebar Find target.
Toolbar creation actions derive from the foreground destination rather than the sidebar mode, while Vault Navigator row menus reuse per-page creation verbs even when that page is not in front.

Window Find routing is chosen by the foreground destination and, within a workspace, its focused pane; page queries belong to their page state, Welcome uses its own content search, and a destination without a searchable target offers no toolbar Find.

Find commands target the focused window model, which suppresses pane keyboard claims before activating terminal search and focusing the toolbar control; Welcome redirects focus into its content field and unsearchable destinations do nothing. Toolbar focus ownership is released on explicit user exit so panes may reclaim the keyboard.

On macOS 26+ a background search host contributes system searchable UI without rebuilding the persistent split-view branch; earlier macOS uses an explicit toolbar search field or compact Metrics popover, retaining native field identity and reserving toolbar height even when no Find is offered.

A focused Telnet session resolves to terminal Find and can present search from the command, but the current toolbar findContext terminal branch only binds Serial and SSH sessions, so Telnet has no usable titlebar query binding through that path.
